disagreements.description: Chinese uses before/after a named month without an explicit inclusion rule; Japanese uses inclusive 以前/以降. The boundary month must not be silently normalized across guides. Distinct scenario-start/current-date roles remain intact, including Zhao Yun scenario-start after195-01. Wu date-clause grouping and Shu acceleration remain separately unresolved.

disagreements.description: Chinese requires candidate compatibility close to the player ruler, with no numeric threshold. Japanese requires absence of an associated relationship (有縁関係). These are different predicates, not translations of the same relation; both guides separately state directed dislike exclusions where present.

Chinese requires Chenliu and Puyang, Xiahou Dun loyalty>95 and city order>80. Wiki has no named-city ownership gate, sponsor loyalty>=90 and assigned-city order>=80, and explicitly excludes a candidate whose prohibited ruler is the player. Chinese does not state that employment-ban gate.

Chinese requires Runan and Xuchang, Dian Wei loyalty>95 and order>80; Wiki names no owned cities and uses >=90/>=80. On a non-Cao-Cao defeat, Chinese says free officer and a 3-month ban, while Wiki explicitly places Xu Chu outside player control and states90 days. Months are not converted to days. Wiki explicitly starts a duel and states Cao Cao recruits regardless of its outcome.
Chinese requires Xun Yu loyalty>95 and his city order>80. Wiki requires loyalty>=90 and states no city-order condition.

Chinese requires both Xiapi and Xiaopei; Wiki either city and current month>=195-01. For player Liu Bei, Chinese Mi Zhu merit>10000/loyalty>95 differs from Wiki>=5000/>=90. Chinese globally requires historical-female mode, debuted free/undiscovered Mi, and Liu Bei/Mi Zhu same city and off mission. Wiki instead conditionally checks historical Mi, permits her already serving Liu Bei, states no same-city gate, and applies mission only in the player-Liu-Bei branch. Chinese Mi loyalty100/merit1000 results are player-Liu-Bei conditional; Wiki loyalty100 is historical-mode conditional and merit1000 further requires her not already serving Liu Bei.

sourceReferences.sourceSection: 麋氏と劉備（劉備・麋氏結婚）

disagreements.description: Chinese names Zhou Yu and Zhu Zhi and requires all three actors off mission. Wiki lists only scenario3, day0 and Sun Ce ruler. No Chinese-only actors or gates are added to Wiki.

Chinese separately states at least one debuted candidate and at least one free/undiscovered candidate; it does not explicitly require one same candidate to satisfy both. Wiki explicitly nests both conditions under one candidate. Chinese results recruit free/undiscovered candidates; Wiki only event participants. Liu Bei Chinese requires Guan Yu subordinate and same city with Liu Bei, while Wiki explicitly places both in Runan. Do not repair either quantifier from the other source.

sourceReferences.sourceSection: 小覇王・孫策（周泰、蒋欽、陳武、董襲、凌操仕官）
好漢・劉備（龔都、周倉、裴元紹、劉辟、廖化仕官）

disagreements.description: Chinese adds Chaisang/Jianye/Lujiang ownership and Zhou Yu loyalty>95; Wiki has no named-city gate and loyalty>=90. Chinese failure literally makes Zhang Zhao/Zhang Hong the player ruler’s prohibited rulers for12 months; Wiki makes the player ruler their prohibited ruler for360 days and specifies a city outside player control. Preserve the apparent Chinese reversed direction and the distinct units.

Wiki adds current>=196-01 and allows an existing Sun Jian/Sun Ce force without a player-only gate. Chinese explicitly requires the player Sun-Wu ruler, historical-female mode and both Qiaos debuted. Chinese describes two marriages and loyalty/merit changes; Wiki has no result block. Wiki’s mixed force/free status wording remains ambiguous.

Chinese says the force owns the seal and excludes any other Cheng-named force; Wiki says Yuan Shu personally owns it and excludes only COM Cheng forces. Wiki explicitly gives a player choice and COM acceptance. Chinese lists separate directional friendship rules, including individual below-goodwill and nonallied lines. Wiki groups player-force conditions with AND plus a nested OR, preserves a redundant Han-valuing condition, and separately groups nonplayer eligible forces. Do not turn the Chinese lists into Wiki’s conjunctive selector or resolve runtime diplomatic scope.

Wiki explicitly states Cao Pi belongs to a force; Chinese only refers to that force inside mode-specific clauses. Chinese historical mode requires Cao Pi and Yuan Xi in different forces even when Zhen is unmarried; Wiki places that restriction only in the already-married-to-Yuan-Xi branch. Chinese describes dissolution before new marriage; Wiki describes new marriage first and guards dissolution on an existing Yuan-Xi marriage. These are source presentation orders, not executed sequencing.

sourceReferences.sourceSection: 御曹司一番乗り（曹丕・甄氏結婚）

disagreements.description: Chinese nonopening cutoff is before198-12; Wiki is <=199-12. Wiki’s scenario4 day0 branch explicitly requires both forces; Chinese opening alternative says only scenario4 day0. Wiki explicitly distinguishes scenario!=4 and excludes an associated Cao Cao/Yuan Shao relationship in its later branch; Chinese does not. Wiki enumerates regions, including its literal 陳陽 spelling; Chinese leaves region membership unstated.

Wiki has two distinct observations. First states no elapsed-days gate and current-city order100; second adds>=30 elapsed days and uses assigned-city order100. Chinese states>=30 days and ruler-current-city order100. Both Wiki observations remain separate; neither silently replaces the other.

Chinese gives scheduled-death-year/arrival-of-200 alternatives, identifies Yu Ji as debate opponent, specifies20-year life extension and Sun Quan succession on defeat. Wiki simply gives year>=200, a debate, unspecified life extension on victory and death on defeat; opponent and succession are unstated.

Chinese requires Zhuge Liang age>=20, historical-female mode and Huang Yueying debuted, with free/undiscovered/same-force alternatives. Wiki instead states Zhuge Liang in controlled cities and Huang Yueying in controlled cities (never-served free allowed) or undiscovered, without those age/mode/debut gates. Wiki’s controlling force is implicit. Chinese describes marriage, recruitment and loyalty/merit; Wiki describes no outcomes.

Chinese loyalty<90 differs from Wiki<=95. Wiki explicitly excludes employment prohibition by the player ruler and permits Gan Ning in another player-controlled force; Chinese omits those clarifications. Chinese specifies at least one adjacent city; Wiki states force adjacency without that granularity.

Chinese excludes Xinye plus five Wu cities; Wiki additionally excludes Jiangxia, Xiangyang, Jiangling, Changsha, Wuling, Guiyang and Lingling in its broad Jiangdong definition. Wiki explicitly enumerates its regions, including 陳陽. Chinese requires at least one owner of one of four named cities not allied to Cao Cao; Wiki wording covers forces owning any listed city. Chinese describes a large friendship fall with at least one such owner; Wiki has no outcome block.

Chinese adds Jiangling ownership, player/Yi Ji same city, Yi Ji loyalty>95 and Yi Ji off mission. Wiki uses Yi Ji loyalty>=90, ruler assigned-city order100, and player/Yi Ji both action-unused, without the city-ownership/colocation gates. Chinese states both directional dislikes for Ma Su as well; Wiki states them for Ma Liang/Yi Ji but not Ma Su.

Chinese historical-female mode is a trigger and lists Sun Jian/Sun Ce/Sun Quan in its Sun-family ruler scope. Wiki admits Sun Jian or any Sun Jian blood relative and applies historical-character mode only to recruitment/merit/loyalty outcomes. Chinese combined result describes loyalty before merit; Wiki lists merit then loyalty. Source ordering only is preserved.

Chinese requires player Sun Quan, intelligence<75, loyalty>95 and merit>5000. Wiki requires Sun Quan ruler, intelligence<=70, loyalty>=95 and merit>=5000. Chinese has unqualified 91/89/78 Lu Meng stats and unconditional portrait wording; Wiki keeps an unqualified block with those values and explicit PK89/82/72, raises stats only if higher, and changes portrait only if not changed. Neither guide’s unspecified platform is inferred.

Chinese requires Lu Su as a subordinate in the trigger; Wiki makes his presence only a result guard and additionally requires Zhou Yu ordinary status. Chinese defines lower and higher merit cases but leaves equality unstated; Wiki explicitly gives+2000 when Lu Su merit>=Zhou Yu merit. No equality outcome is invented for Chinese.

Wiki explicitly requires Xuchang alongside Luoyang/Chang’an/Ye; Chinese lists only the latter three. Chinese requires player Cao Cao and Cao Cao/successor off mission; Wiki does not state either gate. Wiki enumerates regional city members; Chinese region names remain unexpanded.

Wiki requires the Later Han emperor to exist, not an independently stated alive predicate; Chinese has no existence gate and requires player Liu Bei. Chinese gives separate nonallied/below-goodwill/named-force diplomacy lines, some mutual; Wiki applies nonallied AND below-goodwill AND the Cao/Cao-relative/emperor-supporter group. Chinese lists strategist merit before officer loyalty, Wiki the reverse. Chinese 江洲 versus Wiki 江州 remains source spelling.

Chinese requires off mission, excludes all other Wei-named forces, and describes accession without an explicit player choice. Wiki requires action-unused, excludes COM Wei forces, and states player choice/COM acceptance. Chinese explicitly kills the emperor after title/name changes; Wiki removes the emperor before title/name changes without saying death. Chinese +20 applies to non-Han-valuing officers; Wiki says Han-ignoring officers only. Chinese diplomacy is separately listed and includes Liu Bei/compatibility; Wiki uses an AND selector and blood relatives. Wiki bonus/diplomacy scope is ambiguous because its source outdents those lines; no canonical scope is selected.

Chinese requires Liu-family king rank; Wiki explicitly says emperor rank and still sets emperor in results. Chinese Liu Bei-or-close-compatibility differs from Wiki Liu Bei-or-blood-relation; cross-ruler not-close-compatibility differs from no-associated-relationship. Chinese adds nonalliance with Cao family; Wiki adds no COM Shu-named force. Chinese says emperor dead while Wiki says absent. Chinese diplomacy lines are separate; Wiki groups them conjunctively. Both sources say Wei may accelerate timing without replacement thresholds, a shared unresolved fact rather than an additional numeric difference.

Chinese requires merit>8000 and a Liu Bei-or-compatible ruler; Wiki uses>=8000 and Liu Bei-or-blood-relative, plus tentative console>=3000. Chinese colocates ruler and both officers in the same city unconditionally. Wiki requires only Zhang Bao/Guan Xing same assigned base and only when the Liu force is player controlled. Console3000 remains a question, not a confirmed replacement.

sourceReferences.sourceSection: 虎の子（張苞・関興義兄弟の契り）

disagreements.description: Chinese has a date OR whose scope over cutoff/elapsed-days is unresolved. Wiki requires cutoff<=221-12 and>=180 scenario days, then additionally>=180 days since Wei accession only if Wei occurred. Chinese explicitly allows Sun Jian as well as his blood relatives; Wiki says related-to-Sun-Jian. Chinese diplomacy uses separate filters and includes all emperor forces/compatible Liu rulers; Wiki has AND filters and excludes Cao family from the emperor alternative. No guide resolves the other’s runtime rule.

Chinese explicitly adds12000 merit; Wiki sets merit to12000. Chinese requires player Sun Quan, loyalty>95 and ordinary status; Wiki has Sun Quan force, loyalty>=95 and status!=strategist. Chinese range endpoints are unspecified; Wiki range notation is preserved as3000–15000. Chinese simultaneously says Lu Meng dead and Sun Quan/Lu Meng/Jiang Qin same city, an internal contradiction absent from Wiki. Chinese destination is ruler current city; Wiki assigned city. Both list at least10 subordinates, so that is not retained as a numeric disagreement.

Chinese contains malformed condition Chengdu/Hanzhong order+15; Wiki explicitly requires order>=95. Chinese Liu Bei-or-compatible ruler and not-compatible opponent differ from Wiki Liu Bei-blood-relative ruler and no-associated-relationship. Chinese says death time not yet arrived; Wiki says scheduled-death year234 not reached. Chinese 永安/江洲 versus Wiki 永案/江州 are preserved without correcting one from the other.

Chinese page12 repeats the heading Wu King although its result makes the ruler emperor and names Wu; this observation’s canonical identity is Wu Emperor. Chinese refers to>=360 days since Wei accession in an unresolved date OR. Wiki refers to>=360 days since Wu King accession only if that event occurred, in addition to baseline cutoff/elapsed gates. Chinese explicitly includes Sun Jian; Wiki blood-relative wording. Wiki adds a no-COM-Wu-name gate and conjunctive diplomacy; Chinese has no name gate and separate diplomacy lines. The prerequisite discrepancy remains unresolved.

Chinese uses scheduled-death-year arrival and explicitly emits death before merit/item results; Wiki names natural death and its parenthetical234 but does not list death as a separate result. Chinese explicitly says strategist not ruler; Wiki says strategist. Chinese merit equality is unstated, while Wiki awards+4000 for Zhuge Liang merit<=Jiang Wei merit. No equality branch or death effect is imported into the opposite source.

Chinese explicitly says no result/change in these opening sections; Wiki has empty or absent result blocks. not-stated is not promoted to no-described-change, and no oath/coalition mechanics are inferred.
Chinese explicitly says the new emperor remains in the prior emperor’s city. Wiki only lists the death and identity replacement, with no location result.

Chinese says debut age reached and free/undiscovered. Wiki says scheduled debut year reached and never-served free/undiscovered. Age/year and general-free/never-served restrictions are preserved as different source predicates rather than normalized.

sourceReferences.sourceSection: 小覇王・孫策（周泰、蒋欽、陳武、董襲、凌操仕官）
好漢・劉備（龔都、周倉、裴元紹、劉辟、廖化仕官）

disagreements.description: Chinese describes sponsor merit before recruitment in successful cases; Wiki lists recruited officer allegiance/stats before sponsor merit. Chinese presents other-ruler loss before win for Xu Chu/Two Zhangs; Wiki win before loss. These are textual ordering differences only, with no runtime ordering claim.

Wiki has one aggregate conditions-only Chain Plot section, conditional on Diao Chan being a historical officer and not-yet-appeared. Chinese has three separately named stages, each requiring historical-female mode and unmarried Lu Bu, with undiscovered/guard-status distinctions,30-day dependencies, an18-month guard duration and detailed assassination/split results. The aggregate is not a fourth executable stage and is not silently equated to one staged event.

Wiki has one aggregate conditions-only section with no blood relation to Liu Bei and ambiguous controlled-city order100 scope. Chinese has three named stages, explicit player Liu Bei, first-visit close compatibility and two dislike exclusions, ruler-current-city order100,30-day dependencies,36-month guard duration and third-visit recruitment details. Wiki does not inherit those stage outcomes or dependencies; no exact one-to-one canonical equivalence is asserted.

Fresh Wiki contains only these three event headings, whereas Chinese supplies trigger and result details. Both source observations are retained under the same event identity, but all Wiki facts stay not-stated. Missing Wiki content is a coverage gap, not evidence that Chinese mechanics are runtime-correct.

Chinese uses same current city for these actors. Wiki recommendations use same assigned base; Qiao/Zhen/Lu Meng sections use same current base. Recommendation public-order references also use assigned city in Wiki where applicable. 都市, 拠点 and 所属 are not silently made equivalent; no runtime location model is presumed.

disagreements.description: Chinese uses emperor death as the Wei result and dead as the later accession/campaign condition. Wiki says the emperor ceases to exist as the Wei result and does not exist as the later condition, without a separately stated death operation. Absence and death are retained as source-specific claims, not automatically equated.
